problem:
Let $V=C[0,1],$ the vector space of functions that are continuous over $[0,1].$ Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t,
$$

find the orthogonal projection of $f(t)=2{t}^{2}$ onto the subspace spanned by $g(t)=6t-3.$
worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $f(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{g(t)}$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{g(t)}\,f(t)=\frac{⟨f(t),g(t)⟩}{⟨g(t),g(t)⟩}\,g(t).
$$

 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),g(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2{t}^{2}\cdot (6t-3)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(12{t}^{3}-6{t}^{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & =[3{t}^{4}-2{t}^{3}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =(3-2)-0 \\  & =1,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨g(t),g(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(6t-3)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(36{t}^{2}-36t+9)\,\text{d}t \\  & =[12{t}^{3}-18{t}^{2}+9t]_{0}^{1} \\  & =(12-18+9)-0 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the projection is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{g(t)}\,f(t) & =\frac{⟨f(t),g(t)⟩}{⟨g(t),g(t)⟩}\,g(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (6t-3) \\  & =2t-1.\end{aligned}
$$
